title: After application startup loop fails with "Pump not initialized!" until manual connection to pump initiated
body:
AndroidAPS `f1118e238d-2023.06.11`

Whenever AAPS is (re)started, loop is not functional, failing with "Pump not initialized!" error, until I go into the pump tab and click on the bluetooth status to initiate a connection. Yes, it may be hours in this state before a manual connection will be made, after which everything works.

Pump is an old Dana R.

May or may not be related to https://github.com/nightscout/AndroidAPS/issues/2567

I'm also having this issue (or similar) for a few weeks now. Running 3.1 Master and the loop just wont run for hours on end. I can't figure out when it stops working or why. 
When i open AAPS there is often a delay in showing the BG curve when this happens and the Basal is just on running on preprogrammed Profile levels. But not SMBs no Temp Basals.
This is obviously very aannoying and has repeatedly caused me unexpected hyperglycemias. 
What should i do ? Re-build the app ? 
AAPS has all the bakground permissions and Play Protect is off. S22+, OP_Dash, Libre 3

I can confirm heavy connection/BLE issues on Android 13 using AAPS 3.0.0.1 + ruffy+ combo and sometimes acceptable BLE issues on Android 13 using AAPS 3.2 dev + combo with integrated pump driver. The connection issues could be acceptable if it happens 2-3 times per week. But in addition I experience that the Pump Alarm sound/notification is not triggered at all. This leads to several hours of unexpected hypos due to the missing alarm. Should I raise another issue for this or use this issue? I can provide logfiles of 30 minutes of operation with a threshold set to 30 mins and no alarm is triggered. Sensor alarms are triggered, this is working well.

....and just as I said that, after a few cycles of doing nothing, and seeing "pump not initialized" message in logs, it seems to have managed to connect and issue SMB without me clicking on the pump connection. I'll observe more and report.

OK, it takes a few minutes, but it does connect to pump and succeeds with dosing changes after an application restart, without me having to manually click on pump connection. Should I close this issue, or is there anything more you want to look at here?
primary reason is that pump disconnects unexpectly which is an error state. AAPS can recover from this state now better
